items.title: Bridging the gap between fast-evolving code libraries and AI models
items.raw_excerpt: I’ve been working on an idea to make coding LLMs much smarter about new or less-known libraries. Right now, when developers use fresh packages or new versions, most AI coding tools fail multiple times because they don’t have context about those APIs—they end up searching the web and hallucinating. My project aims to fix that by indexing packages and version, and exposing them through a unified API that LLMs (or AI agents) can query directly. The system would understand which version the user’s environment uses, explain why a symbol is missing or deprecated, and suggest alternatives or migration paths. Do you think this is a valuable direction for improving AI-assisted coding tools?

items.title: AI 的本质不是算力，而是「上下文革命」
items.raw_excerpt: 过去几年，人工智能的浪潮一次又一次刷新人们的想象：模型变得更大、算力更强、应用更广。 但在光鲜的成果背后，一个更深层的问题被不断暴露 —— AI 真的“理解”世界了吗？它能记住对话，却常常忘记语境，能生成答案，却未必明白问题的由来。人们开始意识到，智能的边界，不在算法，而在语境。 正是在这样的背景下，上交大生成式人工智能实验室（GAIR Lab）提出了一个颠覆性的观点：人工智能的本质不是算力革命，而是“上下文革命”。 他们在最新论文中，把“上下文”从语言模型的附属概念，提升为智能系统的核心结构，认为系统理解世界的方式，取决于它如何吸收、组织并重构语境。 这项研究通过回溯上下文系统的演化历史，结合大量系统实验与理论建模，提出了“上下文工程”（Context Engineering）这一全新学科框架。团队发现，从早期依赖传感器和规则的 Context 1.0，到能够跨模态理解语义的智能体 2.0，AI 的每一次跃迁，都是一次对“语境吸收力”的升级。 在参数增长趋于极限的当下，这项研究像是在为人工智能指明新的出路：当机器不再只是记住语境，而能理解并创造语境，也许，那才是真正的智能时代的开始。 语境，才是智能的真正边界 这篇论文的实验结果揭示了一个重要规律：人工智能的进步，归根结底取决于系统对“上下文”的理解和利用能力，也就是它能多好地吸收、组织和重构语境。 作者通过比较不同代的智能系统，总结出了上下文工程的发展路径。他指出，从最早依赖传感器和规则运行的系统（比如 Context Toolkit、Cooltown），到如今能理解自然语言和多模态信息的智能体（如 ChatGPT、LangChain、Letta），智能的提升，其实就是系统能处理的语境越来越复杂。 早期的系统只能根据明确输入作出反应，而现在的系统已经能通过语义推理理解人类意图，做出更自然的互动，这标志着上下文工程正式进入

Yet behind the impressive achievements, a deeper issue has consistently emerged—does AI truly "understand" the world? It can recall conversations but often forgets context; it can generate answers but may not grasp the origins of questions. People are beginning to realize that the boundary of intelligence lies not in algorithms but in context. It is against this backdrop that Shanghai Jiao Tong University's Generative AI Lab (GAIR Lab) has proposed a groundbreaking view: the essence of AI is not a computing revolution but a "context revolution." In their latest paper, they elevate "context" from a peripheral concept in language models to the core structure of intelligent systems, arguing that how a system understands the world depends on how it absorbs, organizes, and reconstructs context. By tracing the evolution of context systems and integrating extensive experiments with theoretical modeling, the research introduces a new disciplinary framework called "Context Engineering." The team found that from the early Context 1.0, reliant on sensors and rules, to the intelligent agent 2.0 capable of cross-modal semantic understanding, each leap in AI represents an upgrade in "context absorption capability." As parameter growth approaches its limits, this research seems to chart a new path for AI: when machines no longer just remember context but can understand and create it, perhaps that marks the true dawn of the intelligent era.

Pero detrás de los brillantes logros, un problema más profundo se ha expuesto continuamente: ¿realmente la IA "comprende" el mundo? Puede recordar conversaciones, pero a menudo olvida el contexto; puede generar respuestas, pero no necesariamente entiende el origen de las preguntas. La gente comienza a darse cuenta de que el límite de la inteligencia no está en el algoritmo, sino en el contexto. Es en este contexto que el Laboratorio de Inteligencia Artificial Generativa de la Universidad Jiao Tong de Shanghai (GAIR Lab) propuso una perspectiva disruptiva: la esencia de la inteligencia artificial no es una revolución de la potencia de cálculo, sino una "revolución del contexto". excerpt_i18n.en: Where are the boundaries of AI? What can it do, and what can't it do? Is it 100% accurate? Amid the AI wave, vendors and businesses are navigating through uncertainty. The puzzle of AI applications resembles the challenges faced by CRM a decade ago. "AI is even more difficult than CRM because CRM has certainty, with clear processes and rules leading to visible outcomes, but current AI hasn't reached that level yet," Liu Kang, Senior Product Director at Fenxiang Xiaoke, told Leifeng Wang. To what extent must AI and CRM integrate to become an effective and user-friendly business system? In the marketing field, the evaluation "Digital Native Applications & AI-Powered Marketing Capability Requirements Based on Large Models," initiated by the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology (CAICT), might serve as a reference standard to assess AI application capabilities amid the confusion. CAICT's evaluation criteria cover multiple dimensions, including data capabilities, marketing automation, and scenario adaptability. As the only CRM vendor to pass this evaluation, Fenxiang Xiaoke offers a solution with its enterprise-grade intelligent CRM platform ShareAI, embodying "AI + CRM + industry expertise." Transitioning from reactive AI to AI-native CRM, historically, CRM systems were often defined as "customer-centric operational management tools"—management meant record-keeping, where vendors collected data and processed it according to the company's standardized workflows. For example, in sales scenarios, this structured data processing conflicts with the unstructured language data common in most sales contexts, preventing CRM systems from effectively serving businesses.
